extra.message: SQLinjection.run() builds a SQL query by directly concatenating the unsanitized 'id' query-string parameter into cursor.execute(): "SELECT ... WHERE id=" + id. An attacker can supply id=1 UNION SELECT ... or id=1 OR 1=1 to exfiltrate all rows or break the query, resulting in classic SQL injection.

AuthBypass.run() sanitizes 'username' with a whitelist regex but concatenates the raw, unsanitized 'password' parameter directly into the SQL string: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='" + username + "' AND password='" + password + "'". A password value like ' OR '1'='1 bypasses authentication entirely (classic SQLi auth bypass).

XSSReflected.run() returns the raw 'msg' query-string parameter unescaped as 'content', which is later formatted directly into the HTML page template (handlers.py TemplateHandler.get_content). No HTML-escaping (e.g. html.escape) is applied, allowing arbitrary script injection, e.g. /post?msg=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>.

XSSStored.run() inserts the raw 'comment' parameter into the database (parameterized, safe) but when rendering stored comments back it interpolates each column value directly into '{}'.format(column) without HTML-escaping. Any comment containing HTML/JS is persisted and later executed in every visitor's browser -- classic stored XSS via the guestbook.

UnvalidatedRedirect.run() takes the 'path' parameter and inlines it, unvalidated and unescaped, into a client-side redirect script: window.location.replace('{path}'). There is no allow-list/same-origin check, enabling open redirect (path=http://evil.example) and, because the value is not escaped, JavaScript-context injection by closing the string literal (path=');alert(document.cookie);//) for DOM-based XSS.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: CommandInjection.run() builds a shell command string by joining a static command ('host'/'nslookup') with the raw, unsanitized 'domain' parameter and executes it via subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True). An attacker can supply domain=;ifconfig (or any shell metacharacters) to execute arbitrary OS commands.

UnsafeDeserialization.run() calls pickle.loads() on attacker-controlled, base64-decoded 'object' parameter. Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted object implementing __reduce__ (as demonstrated by the class's own RCE helper at lines 178-181 that calls os.system).

PathTraversal.run() takes the 'path' parameter and opens it directly with os.path.abspath(path) without restricting it to a base/allowed directory. An attacker can supply path=/etc/passwd or path=../../../etc/passwd to read arbitrary files on the filesystem readable by the server process.

SessionFixation.run() accepts a 'session' value directly from the query string and sets it as the SESSIONID cookie: cookie['SESSIONID'] = session, with no regeneration or validation. An attacker can pre-choose a session identifier, trick a victim into using it (e.g. via a crafted link), and then hijack the victim's authenticated session once AuthBypass associates that session id with the victim's account.

AuthBypass.run() contains a hardcoded backdoor credential check: if username == 'dsvpwa' and password == 'dsvpwa', granting a default authenticated session regardless of the users database. This hardcoded credential provides a universal authentication bypass.

XSRequestForgery.run() performs a state-changing action (updating the user's email address) on a plain GET request, gated only by the SESSIONID cookie with no CSRF token or SameSite protection. An attacker can embed a link/image such as /settings?email=attacker@evil.com on a third-party page; any logged-in victim who loads it has their email silently changed (classic CSRF).

The settings form renders user[2] (firstname), user[3] (lastname) and user[4] (email) directly into the 'value="{}"' HTML attribute of input elements without HTML-escaping. Since the email field can be set to arbitrary attacker-controlled text via the adjacent CSRF-able update path (lines 322-325), a value like "><script>...</script> breaks out of the attribute and executes stored XSS whenever the settings page is viewed.

Clickjacking.run() performs an irreversible, destructive action (deleting the user's account: DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?) triggered by a plain GET request gated only by the SESSIONID cookie, with no CSRF token. Combined with the missing frame protections (see handlers.py CSP header), this action can be triggered cross-site or via an invisible framed iframe/click.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers

extra.message: VulnHTTPRequestHandler.cookie is declared as a class attribute (a single shared http.cookies.SimpleCookie() instance) rather than being created per-instance/per-request. Because VulnHTTPServer is a ThreadingHTTPServer, every concurrent request thread calls self.cookie.load(...) and mutates this same shared object (do_GET, line 199), so one user's request can overwrite or read another concurrently-connected user's SESSIONID under race conditions, enabling cross-user session confusion/hijacking on a busy server.

cwe: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization (Race Condition)

extra.message: do_BDR() is invoked automatically by BaseHTTPRequestHandler whenever a request uses the custom HTTP method 'BDR'. At risk level 3 it passes self.path[1:] (the full, attacker-controlled request path) directly to subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True) and returns the output. This is a full remote command execution backdoor: any client can send 'BDR /;id HTTP/1.1' to execute arbitrary shell commands.

StaticHandler.find() opens files using open('./{}'.format(path), ...) where 'path' is taken directly from the raw request path (self.path in do_GET, only query string stripped -- no normalization of '..' segments or URL-decoding checks). A request like GET /../../../../etc/passwd escapes the intended static file root and reads arbitrary files readable by the server process.

The SESSIONID token is generated using random.sample(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, 20), which relies on the non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister PRNG. Its output is predictable/reproducible given enough observed samples (or knowledge of internal state), making session tokens guessable and undermining session security; secrets.token_hex/urandom should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak PRNG

extra.message: The Content-Security-Policy header is set to "default-src * 'unsafe-inline'" on every response. This wildcards all sources and permits inline script/style execution, effectively neutering CSP as an XSS mitigation, and includes no frame-ancestors directive, leaving the application open to framing/clickjacking (no X-Frame-Options is set anywhere either).

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers

extra.message: The X-XSS-Protection header is explicitly set to '0' on every response, disabling legacy browser XSS auditor/filter protections and compounding the impact of the reflected/stored XSS findings elsewhere in the app.

When --ssl is enabled, the SSLContext explicitly re-enables options that are disabled by default for security: ctx.options &= ~ssl.OP_NO_SSLv3 (re-allows the broken SSLv3 protocol), ~ssl.OP_NO_COMPRESSION (re-enables TLS compression, exposing CRIME-style attacks), and ~ssl.OP_CIPHER_SERVER_PREFERENCE (lets the client dictate cipher choice). This deliberately weakens the TLS configuration below safe modern defaults.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
